incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: 12 GPU OOMs in last 5m on cluster serving-runtime-prod (shard: us-west-2/gpu-pool-3). Affected model: redwood-7b-v2 (quantized). Paging @Ethan (oncall). https://internal.incidents/redwood/1713456789

Ethan: Acknowledged. Jumping in — will start with node list and recent deploys. Can someone paste the node IDs and recent config changes?

Priya: nodes: gpu-g4-03,gpu-g4-04,gpu-g4-08. We deployed a small batching/kv-cache tweak 18m ago: batcher.max_batch_tokens from 4096 -> 8192 and kv_cache.expiry bumped to 30m.

Maya: Observed spike at ~1713456600 in the trace logs. Errors look like CUDA OOM on allocator alloc_async, stack: runtime/infer/kv_cache.cc:102

Ethan: Pulling nvidia-smi + allocator stats from gpu-g4-03 now.

Ethan: (paste) nvidia-smi sample:
```
GPU 0: 40GB total, 39.6GB used, 0.4GB free
Processes: python(UID:1001) pid:22411  used 39.0GB
nvmlMalloc retries: high
```

Ethan: runtime memory debug dump (summarized):
- total_arena: 40GB
- used_by_tensors: 34.7GB
- fragmentation_overhead: 4.2GB (≈10.5%)
- allocator_internal: 0.7GB
- kv_cache_reserved: 6.1GB (growing)

Priya: Key observation: kv_cache reserved + batcher commit now > previous observed peak. Fragmentation measure spiked after that batching change. Hypothesis A: increasing max_batch_tokens increased transient allocation high-water marks, combined with long-lived kv cache caused fragmentation and left insufficient contiguous blocks.

Luis: Hypothesis B: quantized kernel changes from v2 introduced different allocation patterns (smaller but more numerous allocations) and made fragmentation worse. We rolled quantized runtime last week.

Maya: Agree on A+B. We have two levers to test live: 1) tighten max_batch_tokens back to 4096 (fast config flip), 2) reduce kv_cache.expiry to 5m or evict cold prefixes. Which do we want first?

Ethan: Do config flip 1 first (low-risk). I'll push batcher.max_batch_tokens=4096 for pool us-west-2/gpu-pool-3 and watch. Also throttling new requests to the quantized model via routing: set route weight redwood-7b-v2 -> 0.2, fallback to redwood-7b-v1.

deploy-bot: Applying route change: redwood-7b-v2 weight set to 20% for production; redirect 80% to redwood-7b-v1. Change ID: route-20240417-01

Ethan: Pushed batcher.max_batch_tokens rollback on gpu-g4-03/gpu-g4-04/gpu-g4-08. Watchers: @Priya @Maya please watch OOM counts.

Priya: Seeing immediate drop in OOMs on g4-03 within 90s. OOMs moved from 3/min -> 0/min on that node. Fragmentation % dropping (quick sample): before: 10.5% -> now: 4.6%.

Maya: GPU free increased to ~1.8GB on g4-03. Latency for some requests increased by ~20ms due to routing to v1, but error rate down. Customer impact: 2% of tail calls were errors during peak window, primarily on streaming sessions that hit large batch combos.

Luis: We should still capture heap / pmap from the workers that OOMed for full RCA. Can someone run the memory-inspect script and attach raw logs? e.g., /opt/runtime/tools/mem-inspect --output /tmp/mem-g4-03.log && paste.

Ethan: Uploaded /tmp/mem-g4-03.log to incident bucket: s3://incidents/1713456789/mem-g4-03.log

Priya: I pulled the log. Key excerpts:
```
Allocator arenas: 6
Largest free block: 1.2GB
Free segments scattered across 400MB chunks
KV cache live objects: 1.9M prefixes (~6.1GB)
Batcher transient high-water: 7.9GB (peak)
Recent frees show non-contiguous small blocks -> fragmentation
```

Maya: Timeline so far:
- 1713455580: Canary for quantized runtime rolled to 50% (last week)
- 1713456400: Batching/kv-cache config changed (max_batch_tokens 4096->8192, kv_cache.expiry 30m)
- 1713456600: Latency spike and first OOMs start
- 1713456789: Incident triggered by incident-bot
- 1713456900: Rollback max_batch_tokens -> 4096 + route shift to v1
- 1713457000: OOM rate falls to baseline

Ethan: Short-term mitigation summary (do not remove):
- Rolled batcher.max_batch_tokens back to 4096 on affected pool
- Reduced redwood-7b-v2 traffic to 20% via routing (fallback to v1)
- Restarted affected worker process on g4-04 with mem-check enabled (no longer OOMing)

Priya: Next steps for full RCA (owners):
- Priya: run longer-term kv cache profiling to find growth modes + add eviction heuristics (owner: Priya)
- Luis: run allocator stress test with quantized v2 to reproduce fragmentation pattern (owner: Luis)
- Maya: instrument batcher to record transient peak per-request (owner: Maya)
- Ethan: coordinate customer comms summary for postmortem (owner: Ethan)

Luis: Quick mitigation idea for future: allow runtime to request contiguous memory defrag (e.g., prefetch + compaction) or split large allocations into smaller sub-allocations with internal pooling. Will prototype in sandbox.

Maya: For the post-incident alerting: create detector combining (kv_cache_reserved_growth > 2GB in 10m) AND (transient_batch_peak > 6GB) -> paged before hard OOM. That would have flagged earlier.

Ethan: Handing off to Priya for RCA write-up and follow-up. I'll be available for any clarifying Qs. Priya, take the lead for the next oncall window.

Priya: Taking over. ETA for full RCA draft: 48h. Will include timelines, logs, reproduction steps, and recommendations (batching caps, kv eviction, defrag work).

Maya: Notes attached: links to traces and charts: https://observability.internal/redwood/trace/1713456789 and dashboards: https://dashboards/internal/ooms/1713456789

Ethan: Closing incident thread once RCA posted. Marking severity: Sev2 (partial customer impact, mitigated).

incident-bot: Incident 1713456789 status change -> mitigated by team actions. Severity: Sev2. Assigned RCA: Priya.

Priya: Will post RCA doc here when ready. Thanks all for quick triage. :tada:
